author: Contributor 62
about: Expo reference concrete sends, ordered tickets, mixed tickets, receipt lookups, payload validation and error/retention rules. Each excluded documented provider, authorization, native presentation or network rule is explicitly source-linked and recorded against the online, correctly provisioned, no-enhanced-security configuration. Setup phones represent native registration; exact undocumented validation codes/messages are not asserted.

notReplayed.pushGetReceipts#doc MessageRateExceeded: The World has online providers with no per-device rate-fault configuration. This receipt error is possible in the real gateway but no demanded caller or life selects its cause.
notReplayed.pushGetReceipts#doc MismatchSenderId: The native-registration door represents correctly provisioned FCM recipients. No provider credential/sender configuration is exposed by this pack.
notReplayed.pushGetReceipts#doc InvalidCredentials: The modeled providers are correctly provisioned; credential revocation/EAS credential repair are excluded, with no provider-credential configuration mechanism.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc missing provider credential: The devices door assumes correctly provisioned projects. No credential-missing provider configuration or fault mechanism is modeled.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc TOO_MANY_REQUESTS: This World has no project-wide traffic-load/rate-fault configuration. The kernel deploy allowance is a separate concern, and this local gateway does not synthesize that real-service error.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc transient HTTP 429 and 5xx: The reference is advice for a temporarily unavailable service. The online gateway has no downtime/fault configuration; RH2 performs one timed fetch rather than these SDK retries.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc enhanced security UNAUTHORI: Enhanced push security is disabled in the measured RH2 caller and native project configuration. Access-token setup and an authorization-fault mechanism are excluded.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc background configuration an: Background app tasks/configuration and precedence when both flags are supplied are excluded; RH2 sends foreground-style title/body notices. Payload preservation is not background execution.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc TTL expiration and preceden: The simulated devices are always online; offline redelivery, expiry scheduling and the providers own four-week default TTL are excluded. The fields may be carried as payload, without simulating scheduling.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc priority defaults and sleep: Devices are online and awake. Native default priorities, platform-specific delays, doze and battery policy are excluded. A typed priority can be carried without claiming provider scheduling.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc custom sounds and permissio: Native sound-file installation and ios.allowsSound/ios.allowsBadge permission settings are excluded. Inbox is payload inspection, not a native sound or badge engine.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc badge clearing: Persistent OS badge state and sound/badge permission effects are excluded. The published badge payload is replayed, but setting an OS badge is not modeled.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc notification channels: The online simulated phone has no native Android channel registry or default-channel creation mechanism. RH2 sends no channelId; channel configuration is excluded.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc rich images: Image fetching, native rich-notification extensions and provider transformation are excluded; no file/media delivery or native extension mechanism is modeled.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc collapse tag and thread gro: Offline collapse, Android tag replacement and iOS thread grouping are excluded; inbox is a chronological payload log, not a native notification tray.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc iOS presentation and native: iOS interruption levels, Focus/filter criteria, target windows/relevance scores, native category actions and mutableContent extensions are excluded. The scope does not provide native presentation/configuration machinery.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc platform icon defaults: Native drawable/icon installation and icon defaults are excluded; the gateway does not render native notification widgets.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc gzip request transport: Gzip decoding is implemented by the kernel manifest encoding. The page provides no literal compressed request fixture to transcribe; blind/standalone clients and kernel transport checks cover bytes separately.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc format pseudocode: The format blocks contain non-JSON type expressions such as status unions and string placeholders. They specify shapes rather than executable requests; the concrete single/batch examples and derived schemas cover those shapes.
notReplayed.pushGetReceipts#doc receipt format pseud: Receipt ID keys, string[] and status unions are format pseudocode, not executable request fixtures; concrete lookup examples and derived schema cover the format.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc delivery guarantee and offl: Real-provider retries, offline delivery and end-user confirmation are excluded. This simulation explicitly assumes online phones and equates its provider acceptance with its own inbox display, not real delivery proof.
notReplayed.pushSend#doc network diagnostics and con: DNS, traceroute, TLS diagnostics and SDK connection/backoff tuning are caller/network troubleshooting rather than push API fixtures. No external network diagnostic or SDK pooling mechanism is modeled by the pack.
